These read only bits are used by the Sequencer to communicate status to the outside world. Bit 8 is also used as Sequencer interrupt, with the complement of this bit OR-ed into the Run bit in PKA_FUNCTION

A 1b indicates a mismatch was detected between bits 28:24 of a Sequencer instruction word and the Hamming protection code calculated from bits 23:0 of that same instruction word. This Hamming code detects at least 2 bit errors in bits 23:0. The state of this bit is OR-ed into the protection_int output of the engine
A 1b indicates parity error was detected
When 1b is returned this read only bit indicates that the zeroization logic is busy. During zeroization the PKA cannot be used

This bit is set to 1b when the main Sequencer receives a SW reset during a complex operation, thereby unlocking the Sequencer. The bit is sticky: It can be cleared again by writing a 1b to this location. Writing a 0b has no effect
